intro: Purpose beyond para que: formal connectors, a que after verbs of movement, and no sea que.
p.a que: so that (after a verb of movement)
b1.texto:
With **one subject**, purpose is a preposition + **infinitive**: **para**, **a fin de**, **con el fin de**, **con el objeto de**, **con vistas a**.

With **two subjects**, add **que** + **subjunctive**: **para que**, **a fin de que**, **con el fin de que**, **con el objeto de que**.

The tense follows the main verb: lo **hago** para que **estés** contento; lo **hice** para que **estuvieras** contento.

After a verb of movement (ir, venir, salir, subir, bajar) Spanish uses **a**: vengo **a** verte; vengo **a que** me **expliques** esto.

After a command, a bare **que** can express purpose: acércate, **que** te **vea**.

**No sea que** + subjunctive is in case something unwanted happens: llévate el paraguas, **no sea que llueva**.

**¿Para qué?** asks for the purpose. **¿Por qué?** asks for the cause.
b3.titulo: A notice from the town hall
b3.f0: The town hall has taken several measures in order to improve the traffic.
b3.f1: The centre will be closed to cars so that residents can walk around.
b3.f2: There will be more buses with the aim that nobody needs a car.
b3.f3: Technicians will go to the neighbourhoods so that residents can tell them their problems.
b3.f4: Leave in good time, in case you find streets closed.
b5.pregunta: Complete: I did it so that you would be happy.
b5.o0.refuerzo: A past main verb takes the past subjunctive.
b5.o1.refuerzo: Estés follows a main verb in the present.
b5.o2.refuerzo: Para que always takes the subjunctive.
b6.pregunta: Complete, one subject: they took measures in order to improve the traffic.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Without que you need the infinitive.
b7.pregunta: Complete: I've come so that you can explain this to me.
b7.o0.refuerzo: After a verb of movement: a que.
b8.o0: Take the umbrella, in case it rains.
b8.o1: Take the umbrella, since it isn't raining.
b8.o1.explicacion: No sea que warns of something that may happen.
b8.o2: Don't take the umbrella unless it rains.
b9.pregunta: What is the difference between «¿por qué?» and «¿para qué?»
b9.o1.refuerzo: Por looks back at the cause, para forward at the aim.
b10.traduccion: The centre will be closed so that residents can walk around.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write a formal proposal to your town council asking for an improvement in your neighbourhood, explaining its purposes.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Present aloud a project at work and explain what each measure is for.
